slides.title: Levers
slides.english_text:
Levers
• We can consider the mechanisms by which muscles act on bones using descriptions based on levers
• Alever is a rigid structure, in this case a bone, that moves on a fixed point called the fulcrum in this case an articulation
• A lever moves when an applied force or effort is sufficient to overcome any load or resistance that would oppose or prevent such movement
• In the body, each bone is a lever and each joint is a fulcrum, and muscles supply the applied forces.
• Movement of the skeleton occurs at joints, so there has to be sufficient muscle power to move all the bones at these joints.

slides.title: Moments & Moment Arms
slides.english_text:
Moments & Moment Arms
• The Moment of a force is a measure of its tendency to cause a body to rotate about a specific point or axis
• The magnitude of the moment of a force acting about a point or axis is directly proportional to the distance of the force from the point or axis
• The moment arm or lever arm is the perpendicular distance between the line of action of the force and the center of moments
• The Center of Moments may be the actual point about which the force causes rotation.

slides.english_text:

slides.title: Dynamic Trunk Stabilization
slides.english_text:
Dynamic Trunk Stabilization
• Static stability refers to the property of maintaining and controlling the body’s orientation in space, usually by keeping the LoG within the BoS
• In any active human movement, some components of the body are stabilized so that other components can move
• The body has to maintain postural control during dynamic activities
• The key to achieve postural control is actively contracting the most central muscles of the body, i.e. the core muscles
• Dynamic trunk stabilization is maintaining the stability of the trunk and the lumbar spine, within a safe range of movement through activation of core musculature, like transverse abdominis muscles

blocks.text: • Static stability refers to the property of maintaining and controlling the body’s orientation in space, usually by keeping the LoG within the BoS
blocks.body_text: Static stability refers to the property of maintaining and controlling the body’s orientation in space, usually by keeping the LoG within the BoS

blocks.text: • In any active human movement, some components of the body are stabilized so that other components can move
blocks.body_text: In any active human movement, some components of the body are stabilized so that other components can move

blocks.text: • The body has to maintain postural control during dynamic activities
blocks.body_text: The body has to maintain postural control during dynamic activities

blocks.text: • The key to achieve postural control is actively contracting the most central muscles of the body, i.e. the core muscles
blocks.body_text: The key to achieve postural control is actively contracting the most central muscles of the body, i.e. the core muscles

blocks.text: • Dynamic trunk stabilization is maintaining the stability of the trunk and the lumbar spine, within a safe range of movement through activation of core musculature, like transverse abdominis muscles
blocks.body_text: Dynamic trunk stabilization is maintaining the stability of the trunk and the lumbar spine, within a safe range of movement through activation of core musculature, like transverse abdominis muscles

slides.title: Proper Body Mechanics
slides.english_text:
Proper Body Mechanics
• Body Mechanics: the wayin which we position our bodies during tasks
• Because our bodies are subject to the principles of biomechanics
• How we position our bodies affects the efficiency of our movements & the stress that is placed on the body tissues
• During all patient interaction, the caregiver should position himself using the best body mechanics possible to maximize the ability to accomplish the task with minimal effort in a safe manner

slides.title: Patient position
slides.english_text:
Patient position
To achieve good body
mechanics in the transfer
task, the patient:
• Moves forward in the chair, decreasing the distance between patient & caregiver
• Place the feet under the CG and slightly apart to maximize the BoS BoS
• Leans forward so that the LoG is as close as possible to the BoS
• Places the hands on the armrests

Caregiver position
• Toachieve good body mechanics in the transfer task, the caregiver:
• Closes the distance between the caregiver and the patient by:
• Bringing the feet into or close to the patient’s BoS
• Flexing the trunk so that the caregiver is leaning slightly toward the patient

slides.title: Positioning for stability
slides.english_text:
Positioning for stability
• The caregiver’s BoS is large. The CG of the caregiver is low and over the BoS.
• The patient’s CG is low & moving forward to be over the center of BoS
• The distance between the caregiver and the patient is decreased as much as possible while allowing for necessary movement

slides.title: Directing Forces by Blocking the knees
slides.english_text:
Directing Forces by Blocking the knees
• During standing or partial standing for a transfer, if the patient cannot generate sufficient internal force to maintain the knee in extension.
• The caregiver may apply an external force, “blocking the knee” to assist the patient to stand.
